caption: AND with real signal inputs: a torch stands on each input block, so each goes out when its input turns on; the dust between them is then off exactly when both inputs are on, and the wall torch hanging under that dust turns it back into AND. 4 gt, 5 blocks.

NOT gate, 1 block: a wall torch hanging on the input block itself. The input powers that block, the torch goes out, and the torch is the output: lit exactly when the input is off. A row of them side by side inverts a whole bus.

NAND gate, 2 blocks: a wall torch hanging on each input block, and the output lamp touching both torches. Each torch goes out when its own input is on, so the lamp stays lit unless BOTH inputs are on.

IMPLY gate (A implies B), 3 blocks, glitch-free: the output lamp touches a wall torch hanging on input A (lit while A is off) and the repeater that input B arrives on. The repeater gives B the same 2 ticks the torch takes, so switching both inputs at once never blinks the lamp.

IMPLY gate (B implies A), 3 blocks, glitch-free: the mirror of gate-imply. The output lamp touches a wall torch hanging on input B (lit while B is off) and the repeater that input A arrives on; the repeater gives A the same 2 ticks the torch takes, so switching both inputs at once never blinks the lamp.

NIMPLY gate (A and not B), 4 blocks: a subtract comparator reads input A's block behind it and, at its side, a dust lying against input B's block; it passes A minus B, so the output lights only while A is on and B is off.

NIMPLY gate (B and not A), 4 blocks: the mirror of gate-nimply. A subtract comparator reads input B's block behind it and, at its side, a dust lying against input A's block; the output lights only while B is on and A is off.

XOR gate, 16 blocks, 2 ticks: two subtract comparators, each with one input behind it and the other at its side, so each lights only when its own input is on alone. The side feeds cross in height instead of around each other: a dust lying ON input A's block reaches the upper comparator's side, and a dust UNDER input B's block reaches the lower one's, each at full strength because it touches the powered input block itself. The lower comparator lights the lamp directly; the upper one powers a block whose dust climbs over the core (across the stone that keeps A's dust from joining it, then down a stone sitting on the lower comparator) onto the lamp.
XNOR gate, 18 blocks, 4 ticks: the 16-block XOR whose two signals meet on a stone instead of the lamp; a wall torch on that stone is the output, lit unless exactly one input is on.
OR gate, 1 block, instant: a dust lying on input B's block points into the output, and input A's block sits right beside the output too. Either powered input block lights the output, with no delay.

NOR gate, 2 blocks: a dust lying on input B's block points into input A's block, so A's block is powered whenever A or B is on; the wall torch hanging on A's block is the output, lit only while both are off.
